notes: BATCH Y (lactulose, macrogol, senna, bisacodyl, ispaghula-senna, loperamide, racecadotril). All seven have UK product information; none is no-uk-product. (1) ispaghula-senna: the clinic product (Agiolax) is not on emc or MHRA products under that name; the UK product with the same composition (ispaghula seed + husk + senna fruit granules) is used (emc-102511). (2) racecadotril: no emc entry, but MHRA products has UK SPCs for the 10 mg and 30 mg granules (PL 39418/0001 and /0002), found through the public search index used by products.mhra.gov.uk. (3) Senna, bisacodyl and loperamide each have two UK SmPCs for the same dosage form with different age limits (pack licences): senna adult-labelled pack says not under 18 (outside 4.3) while the 12-plus pack contraindicates under 12; bisacodyl adult tablets say not under 18 while the 12-plus tablets say not under 12; loperamide OTC capsule contraindicates under 12 (max 12 mg/day) while the POM capsule contraindicates under 9 (max 16 mg/day, 9-12 years dosing). Each is a separate formulation so rules do not merge. (4) CONFLICTS: senna and ispaghula-senna SmPCs contraindicate pregnancy and lactation, while BUMPS (pregnancy) and SPS (breastfeeding) say stimulant laxatives/senna and ispaghula can be used; kept as separate rules. Bisacodyl SmPC says not in pregnancy or breastfeeding unless benefit outweighs risk; SPS says it can be used in breastfeeding. (5) Loperamide was NOT added to group:opioid although its SmPC says 'Loperamide is an opioid with low bioavailability and limited potential to penetrate the blood brain barrier at therapeutic doses'; adding it would fire CNS/respiratory-depression rules written for systemic opioids. Integrator may decide. A new group 'antipropulsive' holds loperamide. (6) Loperamide 4.5 names itraconazole, ketoconazole, gemfibrozil, quinidine and ritonavir (not in the master list) - kept in text only, not mapped to group:cyp3a4-inhibitor because the SmPC attributes the effect to combined CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition by those named drugs. (7) Racecadotril 4.5 names ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II antagonists and gliptins as 'not recommended' (bradykinin-mediated angioedema); mapped to group:ace-inhibitor, group:arb and group:dpp4-inhibitor. Clinic products are the paediatric granules only. (8) BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). SPS has no loperamide breastfeeding page (404); none used. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker): the senna, ispaghula-senna and bisacodyl SmPC adrenocorticosteroid (hypokalaemia) interaction is now mapped to the systemic corticosteroids prednisolone and dexamethasone by id instead of group:corticosteroid, so it no longer fires for nebulised/inhaled corticosteroids. Loperamide dysentery and pregnancy rules split by source (OTC capsule contraindicated vs POM capsule should not be used alone; SmPC vs BUMPS); bisacodyl breastfeeding split SmPC vs SPS.
